subtitle: How a Rajput Hero Was Rewritten Across the Centuries

panels.shot: epic low-angle of Chand Bardai’s towering figure silhouetted against a sky of swirling manuscripts and rajput forts fading into mist
panels.action: Chand Bardai stands on a palace terrace, veena resting by his side, as ghostly pages of the Prithviraj Raso whirl around him, morphing into different Rajput forts and royal courts across the centuries.

dialogue.text: Four centuries after Prithviraj fell, Chand Bardai’s Prithviraj Raso was born—and over three more centuries, Rajput courts kept reshaping the hero they needed.

i18n.hi: पृथ्वीराज के गिरने के चार सौ साल बाद चंदबरदाई की ‘पृथ्वीराज रासो’ जन्मी—और अगले तीन सौ साल तक राजपूत दरबारों ने अपने हिसाब से नायक को ढालते रहे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on an open palm-leaf manuscript under lamplight, the name ‘Prithviraj’ freshly inked, with Chand Bardai’s shadow falling across it
panels.action: A palm-leaf manuscript lies on a low wooden desk in a dim chamber, fresh ink forming the name of Prithviraj as the shadowed profile of Chand Bardai leans over, poised with stylus and calm intensity.

dialogue.text: Across North India people say: Chand Bardai saw Prithviraj with his own eyes and wrote his deeds. But the oldest Raso we can hold in our hands was copied only in 1610.

i18n.hi: उत्तर भारत भर में लोग कहते हैं: चंदबरदाई ने पृथ्वीराज को खुद देखा और उसके काम लिखे। पर जो सबसे पुरानी रासो हस्तलिपि हमारे हाथ में है, वह सिर्फ १६१० में नकल की गई थी।

panels.shot: wide archival-style shot of a 17th-century manuscript room in Rajasthan, with scribes at work amid stacks of bound folios
panels.action: Inside a Rajput court library, several scribes sit cross-legged, carefully copying thick bound folios by lamplight, while attendants stack older, worn manuscripts against carved stone walls.

dialogue.text: Historians found the trail in the papers. The earliest surviving Prithviraj Raso manuscript, dated 1610, appears not in the twelfth century, but in a Rajput world already shaped by Mughal power.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकारों ने सुराग कागज़ों में पाया। सबसे पुरानी बची ‘पृथ्वीराज रासो’ हस्तलिपि, दिनांक १६१०, बारहवीं सदी नहीं, बल्कि मुग़ल ताक़त से ढले राजपूती दौर में दिखती है।

panels.shot: diagrammatic overhead shot of four manuscripts laid out side by side, visibly differing in thickness and script density
panels.action: Four separate manuscript volumes lie on a mat: one slim, one broader, one thick, and one massive, their scripts dense and varied, hinting at the growing bulk of the poem over time.

dialogue.text: From about 1,300 stanzas to more than 16,000, the Raso swelled across four recensions. Each generation added tales, verses, and heroes to the skeleton of an older story.

i18n.hi: करीब १,३०० पदों से बढ़कर १६,००० से ऊपर—रासो चार रूपों में फूलती गई। हर पीढ़ी ने पुराने कंकाल पर नई कथाएँ, नए छंद और नए नायकों की परतें चढ़ाईं।

panels.shot: evocative shot of a 16th-century Rajput court under Akbar’s suzerainty, showing Rajput nobles in Mughal dress yet with Rajput armour displayed behind
panels.action: In a richly decorated hall, Rajput nobles wearing Mughal-style robes sit in council, their shields and swords displayed on racks behind them, as a court poet recites before the throne.

dialogue.text: Around Akbar’s time, Rajput rulers served in the Mughal empire yet guarded their pride. Cynthia Talbot and other scholars argue: this is when Prithviraj’s grand legend really crystallized.

i18n.hi: अकबर के समय के आस-पास, राजपूत शासक मुग़ल साम्राज्य में सेवा करते थे, पर अपना मान संभालते थे। सिंथिया टैल्बॉट और अन्य विद्वान कहते हैं: यही समय है जब पृथ्वीराज की विराट कथा सचमुच जमकर बनी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chand Bardai performing in a Rajput court, musicians behind him, nobles listening intently
panels.action: Chand Bardai stands with veena in hand before a seated Rajput ruler and his nobles, his face lit with fierce devotion as he begins to sing, while drummers and flutists sit ready behind him.

dialogue.text: In these courts, Chand Bardai’s voice is imagined as the perfect bard: loyal, fearless, and Rajput to the bone. Through him, Prithviraj becomes the mirror of each patron’s hopes.

i18n.hi: इन दरबारों में चंदबरदाई की आवाज़ को आदर्श भाट माना गया—अटल, निडर और पूरी तरह राजपूत। उसकी ज़ुबान से पृथ्वीराज हर सरदार की आशाओं का आईना बन जाता है।

panels.shot: cinematic split-scene showing a romantic svayamvara on one side and a scholar’s study on the other
panels.action: On the left, a vivid svayamvara scene shows a veiled princess garlanding a warrior; on the right, a quiet study shows a modern scholar examining manuscripts and notes by lamplight.

dialogue.text: The Raso tells of Sanyogita’s secret love and elopement from Jayachandra’s svayamvara. Yet earlier texts about the Chauhans, like Nayachandra Suri’s Hammira Mahakavya, know nothing of this romance.

i18n.hi: रासो संयोगिता के गुप्त प्रेम और जयचंद के स्वयंवर से भाग चलने की कहानी सुनाती है। पर चौहानों पर पहले के ग्रंथ, जैसे नयाचंद्र सूरी की ‘हम्मीर महाकाव्य’, इस प्रेमकथा को जानते ही नहीं।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of a blindfolded archer aiming at an unseen target, sound waves drawn as faint rings
panels.action: In a stylized battlefield vision, a blindfolded warrior stands tall, bow drawn, listening with intense concentration as faint ripples in the air suggest invisible sound guiding his arrow.

dialogue.text: The Raso sings of Prithviraj striking down Muhammad of Ghor in distant Ghazni with a shabda-bhedi arrow. The dates make it impossible, but the image of a blinded hero hearing his enemy endures.

i18n.hi: रासो गाती है कि पृथ्वीराज ने शब्दभेदी बाण से दूर ग़ज़नी में मोहम्मद ग़ोरी को मार गिराया। तारीख़ें इसे नामुमकिन बनाती हैं, पर अँधा नायक जो सुनकर दुश्मन पर वार करता है—यह तस्वीर ज़िंदा रहती है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a ritual fire-pit with emerging silhouettes of warriors, contrasted against a faint map of Rajput clans
panels.action: At night, a glowing ritual fire-pit flickers as shadowy silhouettes of warriors seem to rise from the flames, while above them a faint outline of Rajput clan territories hovers.

dialogue.text: Agnivansha, the tale of Rajputs born from a sacred fire, appears in the Raso too. It gives Rajput lineages a divine start, but scholars treat it as mythic origin, not record of an actual event.

i18n.hi: अग्निवंश, यानी पवित्र अग्नि से जन्मे राजपूतों की कथा, रासो में भी आती है। यह राजपूत वंशों को दिव्य शुरुआत देती है, पर विद्वान इसे पुरानी मिथक मानते हैं, असली घटना का रेकॉर्ड नहीं।

panels.shot: contrasting shot of Talwar-wielding Rajput warriors and a calm scholar turning pages of Hammira Mahakavya
panels.action: In the foreground, Rajput warriors in mail stand with talwars at rest before a fort; in the background, softened by distance, a scholar sits cross-legged turning the pages of Hammira Mahakavya.

dialogue.text: Nayachandra Suri wrote Hammira Mahakavya around 1400 for a Chauhan patron. He praises Chauhan kings, yet does not mention Sanyogita, the blind-archer tale, or Jayachandra’s supposed treachery at Tarain.

i18n.hi: नयाचंद्र सूरी ने करीब १४०० में एक चौहान सरदार के लिए ‘हम्मीर महाकाव्य’ लिखा। वह चौहान राजाओं की खूब प्रशंसा करता है, पर संयोगिता, अंधे धनुर्धर वाली कथा, या तराइन पर जयचंद की कथित गद्दारी का ज़िक्र नहीं करता।

panels.shot: tight shot on a manuscript margin where two hands from different eras add notes in different scripts
panels.action: A palm-leaf manuscript lies open as one hand in older style adds a neat verse at the margin, and another, centuries later, scribbles a new note in a different script and ink.

dialogue.text: If such stories had already existed, a Chauhan poet in 1400 would almost certainly have used them. Their absence, scholars argue, shows that many famous Raso episodes were later additions.

i18n.hi: अगर ये कहानियाँ तब तक चलन में होतीं, तो १४०० का चौहान कवि उन्हें ज़रूर बरतता। उनका गायब होना, विद्वान कहते हैं, दिखाता है कि रासो की कई मशहूर घटनाएँ बाद की जोड़ हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Chand Bardai’s thoughtful face as scenes of different Rajput courts fade in behind him
panels.action: Chand Bardai’s face is shown in close-up, eyes distant, while translucent images of Mewar, Bikaner, and Amber courts appear behind him like layers of time pressing on his imagination.

dialogue.text: The name ‘Chand Bardai’ becomes a vessel. Under Mewar, Bikaner, Amber and other rulers, his imagined voice gathers new victories, new wrongs, and new ideals of Rajput honour.

i18n.hi: ‘चंदबरदाई’ नाम खुद एक पात्र बन जाता है। मेवाड़, बीकानेर, आमेर और दूसरे राजों के नीचे उसकी कल्पित आवाज़ नए विजय, नए अन्याय और राजपूती मान की नई मिसालें समेटती जाती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of three different Rajput courts, each with a poet gesturing upward as if summoning Prithviraj’s image
panels.action: In a triptych-like scene, three Rajput courts from different centuries show different poets standing before their rulers, each lifting a hand as if calling forth an unseen heroic figure.

dialogue.text: Each court faces its own fears: loss of lands, Mughal dominance, rival clans. Each reshapes Prithviraj as the champion who answers their moment—a defender of dharma, a defier of emperors, a model of loyalty.

i18n.hi: हर दरबार अपनी-अपनी डर से जूझता है—ज़मीन का खोना, मुग़ल दबदबा, प्रतिद्वंद्वी कुल। हर जगह पृथ्वीराज को उस दौर का उद्धारक गढ़ा जाता है—धर्म का रक्षक, बादशाहों को ललकारने वाला, निष्ठा की मिसाल।

panels.shot: historical montage of 19th-century presses, nationalist meetings, and a printed book titled ‘Prithviraj’
panels.action: A montage shows a hand-operated printing press, a group of 19th-century Indian intellectuals debating around a table, and a printed book with ‘Prithviraj’ on the cover resting atop newspapers.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, printers and politicians turn Prithviraj into ‘the last Hindu emperor.’ That title itself is modern, built atop the older Raso legend.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, उन्नीसवीं-बीसवीं सदी में छापेखाने और नेता पृथ्वीराज को ‘आख़िरी हिंदू सम्राट’ बना देते हैं। यह उपाधि खुद आधुनिक है, पुरानी रासो की नींव पर रखी नई इमारत।

panels.shot: juxtaposed panel of Tarain battlefield map and a sober medieval Persian chronicle on a desk
panels.action: A map of the Tarain battlefield lies on a table beside a Persian chronicle open to neat script, with a magnifying glass resting between them, suggesting careful comparison.

dialogue.text: Medieval Persian accounts note Prithviraj’s defeat and Ghuri rule, but do not call him a last defender of a community. The idea of a single ‘last Hindu emperor’ comes much later, in a different political age.

i18n.hi: मध्यकालीन फ़ारसी इतिहास पृथ्वीराज की हार और ग़ोरी राज का ज़िक्र करते हैं, पर उसे किसी समुदाय का आख़िरी रक्षक नहीं कहते। ‘आख़िरी हिंदू सम्राट’ का ख़याल बहुत बाद की, अलग सियासी उम्र की पैदाइश है।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Chand Bardai’s hand writing, with the words physically morphing into different scripts and styles as they extend
panels.action: Chand Bardai’s hand writes the name ‘Prithviraj’ on a page; as the word stretches across, its letters subtly transform into different scripts and flourishes, symbolizing centuries of rewriting.

dialogue.text: So the Raso is both treasure and trap. It preserves Rajput memory and emotion, yet its growing verses show more about the worlds that sang Prithviraj than about the man who died in 1192.

i18n.hi: इस तरह रासो खज़ाना भी है और जाल भी। यह राजपूत यादें और जज़्बात बचाती है, पर इसके बढ़ते पद ज़्यादा बता देते हैं उन दुनियाओं के बारे में जो पृथ्वीराज को गाती थीं, उस आदमी से कम जो ११९२ में मारा गया।

panels.shot: modern-day long shot of a reader in a library between shelves of old manuscripts and history books
panels.action: A contemporary reader sits at a long table in a quiet library, old manuscripts on one side and modern history books on the other, studying both with focused attention.

dialogue.text: To know Prithviraj, we must hold legend and evidence side by side—hearing Chand Bardai’s song with respect, yet listening closely to the silences and changes that tell us how ages remake their heroes.

i18n.hi: पृथ्वीराज को समझने के लिए हमें कथा और सबूत को साथ पकड़ना होगा—चंदबरदाई का गीत इज़्ज़त से सुनते हुए, उन ख़ामोशियों और बदलाओं पर भी कान रखकर जो दिखाते हैं कि हर दौर अपने नायकों को नया रूप देता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Rajput Hero Was Rewritten Across the Centuries
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक राजपूत नायक जो सदियों में फिर से लिखा गया
